rows.text: Hm. Pip, stay down. You're bleeding like a butchered hog.
Hm. Moth, stop rolling in the dirt like a burnt piece of meat.
Hm. That gut wound's festering like bad meat. Stay still.
Hm. It's just a body. Move it or leave it.
Hm. The field's turned into a butcher's scrap pile.
Hm. Stop gorging on raw meat like a starving dog, Moth.
Hm. Stop that screaming. You're acting like a spoiled brat at a banquet.
Hm. Moth, get a jacket before you freeze like a slab of meat.
Hm. Grab a rifle, Pip. Don't let them spoil the morning.
Hm. The bench feels right. Better than a burnt batch of rice.
Hm. Sit in the dirt and eat this stew, Pip.
Hm. Eat the kibble or leave it for the animals.
Okay so Ash is like, totally bleeding everywhere, someone help him!
Okay so Tuk is totally on fire and like, everything is just going wrong today...
Okay so Ash, you look like, totally terrible right now...
Okay so, Tuk, you should like, come inside before you get totally soaked...
Okay so Ash is like, totally gone, and everything is just... so quiet now...
Okay so Tuk is like, totally eating everything in the pantry right now...
Okay so that was like, totally intense, Ash is actually losing it...
Okay so Tuk is like, totally walking away without a jacket and it's freezing out here...
Okay so those guys in the fog look totally scary, like, are they coming for us now...?
Okay so I totally made that, like, it's actually really good...
Okay so eating on the dirt is like totally gross, but at least it's sunny...
Okay so this kibble is, like, totally gross, but it's better than nothing, right...
Moth is down. She has a shoulder wound and is bleeding fast.
Negative. Stop screaming and roll, Lux. You are making a scene.
We have only two herbal packs left. Moth needs more than that.
Stop staring. We need to move the body to the graveyard.
Negative. Moth is dead. One casualty in the east field.
Negative. That is enough meat, Lux. You are making a mess.
Negative. Moth, stop breaking things. That table cost a lot.
Negative. Do not walk into the mountains without a jacket.
Six hostiles approaching north wall. Get to the armory, Moth.
The workbench is working well. Ten levels deep now.
This dirt is not a table, Moth.
Eat the kibble or leave it. It is not a choice.
I think, well, Tuk is bleeding too much, maybe we need to move him?
I think, well, maybe he's actually on fire? Rook, please, stop rolling in the dirt!
I think, well, maybe the infection is spreading, so I should probably check the wound again.
I think, well, maybe Rook should... he shouldn't just stand there like that.
I think, well, maybe... Tuk is actually dead? There's so much blood on the grass.
I think, well, maybe you shouldn't be eating that raw, Rook?
I think, well, maybe that table was already unstable, but the noise is... it's quite loud.
I think, well, maybe he shouldn't go out there without a jacket, it's freezing.
I think, well, maybe they're coming from the north, but I... I don't know.
I think, well, maybe the precision is finally improving, if that's even possible.
I think, well, maybe it's better to eat here than wait for a table?
I think, well, maybe we could try to make something more substantial than kibble?
Lux is leaking too much. Tuk will patch him.
Pip, stop rolling in the dirt and get to the water!
Lux smells of rot. He needs medicine.
Pip, stop staring. The meat is gone and the rain is coming.
Lux is dead in the grass. He did not even bleed enough for Tuk to use.
Eat it all, Pip, but do not choke on the raw stuff.
Lux is making too much noise. He is acting like a wounded animal.
Pip, the wind is biting and you have no coat.
Tribals in the fog. Tuk will find good meat today.
Tuk makes things well. This bench is good.
This kibble is bad meat. Tuk wants something real to chew.
Of course, the violence is quite as unrefined as the food.
Naturally, my dear Ash, one would have thought you might have mastered the concept of fire before attempting to cook.
Of course, my dear Rook, you insist on festering in a bed while the cook remains at the stove.
Of course, my dear Ash, staring at the deceased will not return the blood to her veins.
Of course, the dirt has claimed Rook before the sun has even set.
Of course, my dear Ash, one does not need to devour the raw livestock to satisfy a momentary impulse.
Of course, my dear Nate, one would have thought a tantrum might be a more dignified affair than smashing the furniture.
Of course, my dear Ash, if you intend to freeze to death, do try to do it somewhere more aesthetically pleasing than the gate.
Of course, the morning fog provides the most dreadful stage for a massacre.
Of course you would offer a nod, my dear Ash, as if my mastery of the brush were some common occurrence.
Naturally, my dear Nate, dining upon the dirt is a culinary experience I had certainly not requested.
Of course, my dear Ash, we are expected to find nourishment in this gelatinous sludge and dried refuse.
